subject.title: Android: gateway pairing UX trails iOS (duplicate buttons, no discovered list, buried setup code)

question: Should Android reverse the documented de-duplication and make Settings a complete second gateway-pairing surface, or keep Connect canonical with a lightweight Settings entry point?
rationale: Both approaches are implementable, but the permanent owner of pairing controls affects navigation, duplicated actions and state, documentation, tests, and future Android maintenance.

options.title: Keep Connect canonical
options.body: Add a prominent scanner handoff and diagnostics in Settings while retaining setup-code, discovery, and manual connection controls in Connect.

options.title: Adopt Settings parity
options.body: Approve the linked PR's iOS-like pairing surface and revise Connect responsibilities and Android documentation so the two flows do not compete.

recommendation.title: Keep Connect canonical
recommendation.body: Add a prominent scanner handoff and diagnostics in Settings while retaining setup-code, discovery, and manual connection controls in Connect.
